foodTransitionsStudy.method: Pinned original engine-source inspection, not gameplay observation
foodTransitionsStudy.next: Trace upkeep_kill_unit and city_reduce_size, including size-one destruction and script callbacks. Food-update branches are source-verified; helper outcomes, active rulesets and runtime remain unexamined.

findings.title: Upkeep failure can protect a unit from removal
findings.finding: Without an eligible AAPC_UNIT_UPKEEP action auto performer, upkeep_kill_unit returns false before any forced wipe. Otherwise it executes upkeep actions, optionally wipes a surviving unit, and returns whether the original unit ID is no longer alive. Thus the caller cannot assume every food-upkeep unit is destroyed.
findings.basis: Original pinned source inspection; not decompilation or gameplay observation

findings.title: Population loss repairs assignments and guards script-driven destruction
findings.finding: Zero loss returns true. Loss at least equal to city size emits city_destroyed, checks whether the city still exists before removing it, then returns false. A surviving city loses size, updates borders, caps food to its new capacity, removes specialists before workers, refreshes citizens and worker allocation, and refreshes trade partners. If a reason is supplied, city_size_change is emitted and the return value checks whether scripts left the city alive.
findings.basis: Original pinned source inspection; not decompilation or gameplay observation

findings.title: Classic starvation protects evacuation units
findings.finding: The pinned classic cities ruleset protects the EvacuateFirst unit-type flag from food-upkeep removal, provides no food action list, and enables food_wipe. The ruleset loader maps this configuration to the food-specific upkeep auto performer and the engine wipe setting. In conjunction with the helper early return, protection is checked before forced wiping. Shield upkeep uses a different policy: three ordered actions and no final wipe. These are classic configuration and source branches, not observed play or a rule for every ruleset.
findings.basis: pinned classic configuration and original source inspection; runtime unobserved

starvationStudy.next: Trace auto-performer selection and EvacuateFirst unit declarations, then close the static shortage subsystem coverage matrix. Runtime, action execution and remove_city dependent-object cleanup remain unverified.

protectedUnitReachability.method: Pinned classic unit declarations; static inspection only
protectedUnitReachability.finding: The two classic unit declarations carrying EvacuateFirst are Leader and Barbarian Leader. Both also declare NoHome and uk_food=0. Therefore the protected-unit helper branch does not by itself demonstrate a reachable classic famine scenario for these units: city_populate filters for positive actual food upkeep. Effects and alternate rulesets require further tracing.

forcedActionStudy.method: Pinned original source inspection; not decompilation or gameplay observation

findings.title: Forced-action selection and execution have distinct outcomes
findings.finding: Selection returns the first performer in cause-iteration order whose requirements are active with RPT_CERTAIN, using actor owner, tile, unit, unit type, output and action context. Execution selects again, acquires targets, then iterates alternatives for unit actors. Each target-kind branch checks action eligibility before invoking unit_perform_action. A successful action immediately returns its action descriptor; this is not a survival guarantee. After an unsuccessful attempt, actor death returns null, preventing further attempts. Exhausting alternatives also returns null. Consequently null alone does not distinguish no performer, no successful action, or actor death.

removalStudy.method: Pinned original source inspection; runtime unobserved
removalStudy.finding: wipe_unit delegates to wipe_unit_full, which unloads the doomed unit and its cargo, classifies cargo by unload ability and terrain survival, then removes the carrier. It processes helpless cargo before imperiled cargo, prioritizing EvacuateFirst or GameLoss within each group. Non-helpless cargo can seek another transport; only EvacuateFirst receives the teleport fallback. Unrescued cargo is subsequently removed with transport-loss reason. Starvation increments units_lost, whereas disbanded/used units increment units_used. This describes shared removal branches; it does not prove a food-upkeep carrier can encounter every branch in the classic ruleset.
